follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference: on rounded rows the kept profit comes to $10.03 per $100, vs $10.02 exact.
oneTimers: A one-time deferred tax provision of $218.5M from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (enacted July 4, 2025) — a remeasurement of foreign deferred tax assets — is the main reason the tax provision hit $338M, a 57% effective rate. Non-GAAP results exclude it through a $148.1M income-tax adjustment.

A $141.8M net acquisition-related credit — mostly a gain from revaluing the contingent consideration owed on the IBM QRadar assets after the payment terms were amended in June 2025 — sits inside G&A and is why that line fell to $27M from $140M a year ago.

Share-based compensation of $372.7M and amortization of acquired intangibles of $36.9M are excluded from non-GAAP results — but stock pay dilutes shareholders, and it is the biggest reason GAAP profit ($254M) trails non-GAAP profit ($673M).

On July 30, 2025 Palo Alto signed a definitive agreement to acquire CyberArk for about $25B in cash and stock ($45.00 cash plus 2.2005 Palo Alto shares per CyberArk share). It is not in this quarter's numbers and is expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2026.
otherDetail: Other income of $95M, net — $94.8M of other income, mostly interest income on cash and investments, less $0.2M of interest expense.

segments.name: Subscription & support

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Firewall hardware and appliances shipped to customers.

takeaways.text: Next-Generation Security ARR — subscriptions to its newer software platforms — grew 32% to $5.6B, and remaining performance obligations, contracted revenue not yet delivered, grew 24% to $15.8B, more than 6× this quarter's sales. Management called Palo Alto a 'Rule-of-50' company for the fifth straight year.
takeaways.title: The new platforms are compounding

takeaways.text: Operating profit more than doubled to $497M, but the tax provision jumped to $338M — a 57% effective rate — after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act forced a one-time $219M deferred-tax remeasurement. GAAP net income fell 29% to $254M even as non-GAAP profit rose 29% to $673M.
takeaways.title: The tax line ate the profit

takeaways.text: Full-year revenue reached $9.22B, up 15%, with $3.72B of operating cash flow, and the company said it exited the year past a $10B revenue run-rate. GAAP net income for the year was $1.13B, down from $2.58B only because fiscal 2024 included a $1.6B one-time tax benefit.
takeaways.title: Fiscal 2025 in one line

verdict: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 16% to $2.54B and Next-Gen Security ARR 32% to $5.6B, but GAAP net income fell 29% to $254M — operating profit more than doubled, yet a one-time tax charge from the new One Big Beautiful Bill tax law pushed the tax bill to $338M and swallowed the gain.
